mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the prediction is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
regime_hint: Rising Fed Funds rate in late-cycle tightening
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such Fed rate spikes, or FEDFUNDS does not cross the 4% threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market employment) of at least 2% coincident with a falling UNRATE (unemployment rate) suggests strengthening labor demand, which precedes a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥2% and UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: No significant positive 60-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05) when the labor demand/unemployment condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in GDPC1 (real private consumption) exceeding 3% signals weakening demand, which predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines by >3% in consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in INDPRO (industrial production index) above 105, combined with a positive HOUST (housing starts), indicates supply expansion that precedes a positive S&P 5-day forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both INDPRO > 105 and HOUST rises.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three consecutive months during a post-COVID recovery, it signals accommodative policy and is associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when the low-rate condition persists.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 4% followed by a sustained rise in PAYEMS by 1% over the next two months predicts a positive S&P 60-day forward return as labor market tightness improves.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% and then PAYEMS increases by ≥1% over the next two months
failure_condition: No significant positive 60-day return when the sequence is not followed.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly RSAFS (retail sales) decline of more than 5% predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return due to reduced consumer confidence and spending.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS falls by >5%.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent monthly increases in INDPRO and HOUST exceeding 2% each indicate supply expansion, which precedes a positive S&P 20-day forward return in non-recessionary regimes.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both series rise by >2% simultaneously.
